title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

story.what: The change edits TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo in its key-attribute path. When a property or field uses a different key kind from the earlier members, it now skips that member right after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys. The int-key and string-key member dictionaries now get a key only if it is not already present, so a duplicate key no longer makes Dictionary.Add throw. The change also adds analyzer tests and execution tests for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types, and a README section on opting out of source generation.
story.why: Requirement MP-2234: the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types. Those types are still serialized at run time, so their contract must still be checked. Invalid input such as duplicate keys or mixed key kinds must lead to a reported diagnostic, not an analyzer failure.

touches.note: Skips a member with a mismatched key kind after reporting it, and adds int and string keys to the member dictionaries only when they are not already present, for both properties and fields.
New execution tests: no generated formatter exists for a suppressed type, and the type round-trips with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.
New analyzer tests for diagnostics on suppressed types, duplicate and mixed keys, a non-suppressed duplicate-key case, and the absence of generation-only diagnostics.

claims.text: In both the property loop and the field loop, a member whose key kind (int or string) differs from the first keyed member now hits a continue right after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys is reported. So the member is not added to either member dictionary, and its type is not collected recursively.
